name: NG Character Creation Rules
description: Data-driven character creation taxonomy. Every ancestry, background, class, and trait contributes tags for passive skill checks, NPC reactions, faction prejudice, and dialogue gates.

ancestries.name: Border Human
ancestries.summary: Hard-lived folk from the wet border roads, used to suspicion, hunger, and practical bargains.

ancestries.name: Fair Young Elf
ancestries.summary: A pale, long-lived youth from a fading elven household; graceful, watched closely, and often underestimated.

ancestries.name: Ashen Dwarf
ancestries.summary: A tunnel-born exile whose clan marks were burned away after debt, defeat, or oathbreaking.

ancestries.name: Mire Halfling
ancestries.summary: Small folk of reed villages and drowned lanes, quick to vanish when nobles or soldiers come asking questions.

backgrounds.name: Border Drifter
backgrounds.summary: You survived by reading roads, weather, campfires, and desperate faces.

backgrounds.name: Failed Squire
backgrounds.summary: You learned banners, blades, etiquette, and shame before being cast out of a knightly household.

backgrounds.name: Village Outcast
backgrounds.summary: Your own people decided you were unlucky, dangerous, cursed, or simply too useful to treat kindly.

backgrounds.name: Caravan Guard
backgrounds.summary: You walked beside wagons through rain, mud, toll gates, and ambush country.

backgrounds.name: War Veteran
backgrounds.summary: You came home from a lord's war with habits that peace cannot easily tolerate.

backgrounds.name: Cloister Novice
backgrounds.summary: You copied forbidden marginalia, learned old doctrine, and left before vows could become chains.

backgrounds.name: Mill-Born Laborer
backgrounds.summary: You know the weight of wet grain, split timber, broken gears, and masters who count every breath.

backgrounds.name: Exiled Noble
backgrounds.summary: Your name once opened doors. Now it opens old debts, old knives, and old expectations.

backgrounds.name: Street Informant
backgrounds.summary: You traded secrets before you were old enough to understand how many secrets trade back.

classes.name: Mercenary
classes.summary: A paid blade who treats survival as the only contract that never lies.

classes.name: Scout
classes.summary: A pathfinder, skirmisher, and lookout trained to notice trouble before trouble notices the party.

classes.name: Hedge Knight
classes.summary: A poor oath-bearer with battered mail, old manners, and a blade that must answer for both.

classes.name: Cunning Speaker
classes.summary: A negotiator, liar, mediator, and knife-smile survivor who wins fights before steel leaves the sheath.

classes.name: Mage Apprentice
classes.summary: A half-trained arcanist with more theory than control and enough power to make villagers nervous.

classes.name: Barber-Surgeon
classes.summary: A field sawbones who knows how bodies fail, how fear smells, and how much pain buys truth.

classes.name: Oathbound Warden
classes.summary: A defensive fighter sworn to keep gates, roads, bridges, or people standing when others break.

traits.name: Steady Under Fire
traits.summary: You do not move quickly, but panic has to work hard to move you at all.

traits.name: Quick-Eyed
traits.summary: You catch small movements, false smiles, fresh tracks, and the twitch before a blade comes out.

traits.name: Silver-Tongued
traits.summary: You learned that a soft voice can open locks that steel only ruins.

traits.name: Scarred Veteran
traits.summary: Old wounds make you credible to soldiers and frightening to civilians.

traits.name: Scholarly
traits.summary: You reach for memory, doctrine, and precedent before instinct or violence.

traits.name: Brawny
traits.summary: You were built by labor, hunger, and heavy work rather than lecture halls or silk rooms.

traits.name: Delicate Bearing
traits.summary: You look gentle, refined, or sheltered enough that cruel people misjudge you and careful people notice.

traits.name: Arcane Sensitive
traits.summary: Old stones hum, charms itch under your skin, and the wrong dreams sometimes answer back.

traits.name: Hard to Read
traits.summary: Your face gives little away; priests call it restraint, thieves call it good practice.
